tools.name: search_help
tools.description:
Ask for help using PixelLab MCP tools, workflows, or features.
A knowledge agent searches our docs and returns a concise answer.

question.description: What you need help with (tools, workflows, billing, features, deployment). Include the context you are working in. Max 2000 characters.

tools.name: create_image_pixen
tools.description:
Generate a freeform pixel-art image with the Pixen model.

Pixen is the newer of the two fast generators and holds up better on small
sprites. Pick between the three text-to-image tools like this:
- create_image_pixflux — when you need an init image (img2img), a palette
  given as an image, isometric, or shading control.
- create_image_pixen — this one; cleaner small sprites, bigger canvas.
- create_image_pro — best quality, returns a set of candidates, costs more;
  takes a palette as hex colours (1-bit, Game Boy, PICO-8, NES, Lospec).

Canvas: 16-768 per side and each side must be a multiple of 4; total area
16x16 to 512x512. Below 32 the canvas must be SQUARE, so the small sizes
are 16x16, 20x20, 24x24 and 28x28.

Cost: 1 generation. Generation time: ~10-40 seconds (async).
Poll with get_image(job_id).

description.description: What to draw (e.g. 'ornate iron key', 'mossy stone wall').

width.description: Canvas width in pixels. Must be a multiple of 4; width must equal height when either side is below 32. width x height may not exceed 512x512 = 262,144, so the widest canvases are e.g. 768x340 or 680x384, not 768x384.

height.description: Canvas height in pixels. Must be a multiple of 4; height must equal width when either side is below 32.

no_background.description: Return the subject on a transparent background. True for sprites and items, False for scenes. Up to 256x256 of area (65,536 px, e.g. 256x256 or 512x128); larger canvases are refused with it on.

direction.description: Which way the subject faces (weakly guiding).

project_id.description: Internal Game Builder project context; the finished image is linked after generation.

tools.name: get_image
tools.description:
Get a raw-image result by job id, or a gallery image by `gallery:<id>`.

Returns the image(s) inline plus no-auth download URLs when completed, or
progress/error otherwise. A completed job also reports its gallery save:
the Creator ``asset_id`` once saved, or a failure note (the image is still
delivered) while the save is being retried.

job_id.description: The job id returned by any raw-image tool (create_image_pixflux, create_image_pixen, create_image_pro, edit_image, edit_image_pixen, transfer_outfit, inpaint_image, animate_image, image_to_pixelart, unzoom_image, correct_pixelart, reduce_colors, create_normal_map), or a gallery:<id> from list_images — images made on the website have no job id.

index.description: Return only this frame, inline. Use it to reach frames past the first few of a long animation without fetching a URL.

tools.name: edit_image_pixen
tools.description:
Edit an image with a text instruction on the Pixen model (fast, 1 generation).

Returns YOUR image edited — pose, composition and pixel style are preserved
and only what you asked for changes.

Pick between the two edit tools:
- edit_image_pixen — this one; 1 generation, ~10-40s, ONE frame, input max
  256px per side and output max 256x256 in AREA. The default for a single
  sprite.
- edit_image — pro quality, 10-25 generations, ~30-90s, edits up to 16
  frames consistently in one call, accepts a reference image and inputs up
  to 512px. Worth it for animation frames, a character's directions, or when
  pixen's result isn't good enough.

Sizes: the input is capped PER SIDE at 256 (crop an oversized source —
never rescale pixel art); the output is capped by AREA at 256x256 =
65,536px, so 128x512 is fine but 320x320 is not. Output defaults to the
input's size. BOTH sides of both must be multiples of 4 — a 63x222 sprite
is rejected; pad it with transparent pixels to 64x224 first (padding keeps
the pixel grid, rescaling destroys it). Need a bigger canvas? edit_image
takes inputs up to 512.

Cost: 1 generation. Generation time: ~10-40 seconds (async).
Poll with get_image(job_id).

description.description: What to change (e.g. 'give him a red cape', 'make the armor gold'). Same 1-500 bound the v2 endpoint enforces — an empty one would queue a job and spend a generation with nothing to edit towards.

image_base64.description: Base64 PNG to edit. Max 256px per side, both sides multiples of 4 (pad with transparent pixels, never rescale). PREFER image_url — MCP clients routinely truncate large inline base64.

image_url.description: Alternative to image_base64: an https (or data:) URL to the PNG to edit. PREFER THIS for anything but a tiny sprite. Give one, not both.

width.description: Output width, a multiple of 4. Output AREA must be at most 256x256 (65,536px), so 128x512 is fine but 320x320 is not. Defaults to the input image's width. The model re-renders at this size — it does not rescale.

height.description: Output height, a multiple of 4. Defaults to the input image's height.

no_background.description: Background handling. Default (unset) follows the input: a transparent input stays transparent, an opaque one stays opaque.

project_id.description: Internal Game Builder project context; the finished image is linked after generation.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description:
List your active background jobs (pending + processing).

Use this to find stuck jobs you can cancel with cancel_job.
